title: Barnabas and Saul commissioned + Paul's sermon at Pisidian Antioch

paragraphs.text: Now there were at Antioch, in the church that was [there], prophets and teachers, Barnabas, and Symeon that was called Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen the foster-brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
paragraphs.original: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ κατὰ τὴν οὖσαν ἐκκλησίαν προφῆται καὶ διδάσκαλοι ὅ τε Βαρναβᾶς καὶ Συμεὼν ὁ καλούμενος Νίγερ, καὶ Λούκιος ὁ Κυρηναῖος, Μαναήν τε Ἡρῴδου τοῦ τετραάρχου σύντροφος καὶ Σαῦλος.
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de en Antiocheia kata tēn ousan ekklēsian prophētai kai didaskaloi ho te Barnabas kai Symeōn ho kaloumenos Niger, kai Loukios ho Kyrēnaios, Manaēn te Hērōdou tou tetraarchou syntrophos kai Saulos.

paragraphs.text: And as they ministered to the Lord, and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul for the work whereunto I have called them.
paragraphs.original: λειτουργούντων δὲ αὐτῶν τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ νηστευόντων εἶπεν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον· Ἀφορίσατε δή μοι τὸν Βαρναβᾶν καὶ Σαῦλον εἰς τὸ ἔργον ὃ προσκέκλημαι αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: leitourgountōn de autōn tō kyriō kai nēsteuontōn eipen to pneuma to hagion· Aphorisate dē moi ton Barnaban kai Saulon eis to ergon ho proskeklēmai autous.

paragraphs.text: Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.
paragraphs.original: τότε νηστεύσαντες καὶ προσευξάμενοι καὶ ἐπιθέντες τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῖς ἀπέλυσαν.
paragraphs.translit: tote nēsteusantes kai proseuxamenoi kai epithentes tas cheiras autois apelysan.

paragraphs.text: So they, being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia; and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
paragraphs.original: Αὐτοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐκπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος κατῆλθον εἰς Σελεύκειαν, ἐκεῖθέν τε ἀπέπλευσαν εἰς Κύπρον,
paragraphs.translit: Autoi men oun ekpemphthentes hypo tou hagiou pneumatos katēlthon eis Seleukeian, ekeithen te apepleusan eis Kypron,

paragraphs.text: And when they were at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews: and they had also John as their attendant.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γενόμενοι ἐν Σαλαμῖνι κατήγγελλον τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· εἶχον δὲ καὶ Ἰωάννην ὑπηρέτην.
paragraphs.translit: kai genomenoi en Salamini katēngellon ton logon tou theou en tais synagōgais tōn Ioudaiōn· eichon de kai Iōannēn hypēretēn.

paragraphs.text: And when they had gone through the whole island unto Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-jesus;
paragraphs.original: διελθόντες δὲ ὅλην τὴν νῆσον ἄχρι Πάφου εὗρον ἄνδρα τινὰ μάγον ψευδοπροφήτην Ἰουδαῖον ᾧ ὄνομα Βαριησοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: dielthontes de holēn tēn nēson achri Paphou heuron andra tina magon pseudoprophētēn Ioudaion hō onoma Bariēsou,

paragraphs.text: who was with the proconsul, Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. The same called unto him Barnabas and Saul, and sought to hear the word of God.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ἦν σὺν τῷ ἀνθυπάτῳ Σεργίῳ Παύλῳ, ἀνδρὶ συνετῷ. οὗτος προσκαλεσάμενος Βαρναβᾶν καὶ Σαῦλον ἐπεζήτησεν ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hos ēn syn tō anthypatō Sergiō Paulō, andri synetō. houtos proskalesamenos Barnaban kai Saulon epezētēsen akousai ton logon tou theou·

paragraphs.text: But Elymas the sorcerer (for so is his name by interpretation) withstood them, seeking to turn aside the proconsul from the faith.
paragraphs.original: ἀνθίστατο δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐλύμας ὁ μάγος, οὕτως γὰρ μεθερμηνεύεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, ζητῶν διαστρέψαι τὸν ἀνθύπατον ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως.
paragraphs.translit: anthistato de autois Elymas ho magos, houtōs gar methermēneuetai to onoma autou, zētōn diastrepsai ton anthypaton apo tēs pisteōs.

paragraphs.text: But Saul, who is also [called] Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fastened his eyes on him,
paragraphs.original: Σαῦλος δέ, ὁ καὶ Παῦλος, πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου ἀτενίσας εἰς αὐτὸν
paragraphs.translit: Saulos de, ho kai Paulos, plēstheis pneumatos hagiou atenisas eis auton

paragraphs.text: and said, O full of all guile and all villany, thou son of the devil, thou enemy of all righteousness, wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord?
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν· Ὦ πλήρης παντὸς δόλου καὶ πάσης ῥᾳδιουργίας, υἱὲ διαβόλου, ἐχθρὲ πάσης δικαιοσύνης, οὐ παύσῃ διαστρέφων τὰς ὁδοὺς κυρίου τὰς εὐθείας;
paragraphs.translit: eipen· Ō plērēs pantos dolou kai pasēs rhadiourgias, hyie diabolou, echthre pasēs dikaiosynēs, ou pausē diastrephōn tas hodous kyriou tas eutheias;

paragraphs.text: And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shalt be blind, not seeing the sun for a season. And immediately there fell on him a mist and a darkness; and he went about seeking some to lead him by the hand.
paragraphs.original: καὶ νῦν ἰδοὺ χεὶρ κυρίου ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ ἔσῃ τυφλὸς μὴ βλέπων τὸν ἥλιον ἄχρι καιροῦ. παραχρῆμα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπʼ αὐτὸν ἀχλὺς καὶ σκότος, καὶ περιάγων ἐζήτει χειραγωγούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai nyn idou cheir kyriou epi se, kai esē typhlos mē blepōn ton hēlion achri kairou. parachrēma de epesen epʼ auton achlys kai skotos, kai periagōn ezētei cheiragōgous.

paragraphs.text: Then the proconsul, when he saw what was done, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
paragraphs.original: τότε ἰδὼν ὁ ἀνθύπατος τὸ γεγονὸς ἐπίστευσεν ἐκπλησσόμενος ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: tote idōn ho anthypatos to gegonos episteusen ekplēssomenos epi tē didachē tou kyriou.

paragraphs.text: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos, and came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Πάφου οἱ περὶ Παῦλον ἦλθον εἰς Πέργην τῆς Παμφυλίας· Ἰωάννης δὲ ἀποχωρήσας ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὑπέστρεψεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: Anachthentes de apo tēs Paphou hoi peri Paulon ēlthon eis Pergēn tēs Pamphylias· Iōannēs de apochōrēsas apʼ autōn hypestrepsen eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: But they, passing through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia; and they went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down.
paragraphs.original: αὐτοὶ δὲ διελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Πέργης παρεγένοντο εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν τὴν Πισιδίαν, καὶ εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐκάθισαν.
paragraphs.translit: autoi de dielthontes apo tēs Pergēs paregenonto eis Antiocheian tēn Pisidian, kai eiselthontes eis tēn synagōgēn tē hēmera tōn sabbatōn ekathisan.

paragraphs.text: And after the reading of the law and the prophets the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, say on.
paragraphs.original: μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν τοῦ νόμου καὶ τῶν προφητῶν ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχισυνάγωγοι πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγοντες· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἐν ὑμῖν λόγος παρακλήσεως πρὸς τὸν λαόν, λέγετε.
paragraphs.translit: meta de tēn anagnōsin tou nomou kai tōn prophētōn apesteilan hoi archisynagōgoi pros autous legontes· Andres adelphoi, ei tis estin en hymin logos paraklēseōs pros ton laon, legete.

paragraphs.text: And Paul stood up, and beckoning with the hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, hearken:
paragraphs.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ κατασείσας τῇ χειρὶ εἶπεν· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται καὶ οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, ἀκούσατε.
paragraphs.translit: anastas de Paulos kai kataseisas tē cheiri eipen· Andres Israēlitai kai hoi phoboumenoi ton theon, akousate.

paragraphs.text: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they sojourned in the land of Egypt, and with a high arm led he them forth out of it.
paragraphs.original: ὁ θεὸς τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου Ἰσραὴλ ἐξελέξατο τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν, καὶ τὸν λαὸν ὕψωσεν ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ ἐξήγαγεν αὐτοὺς ἐξ αὐτῆς,
paragraphs.translit: ho theos tou laou toutou Israēl exelexato tous pateras hēmōn, kai ton laon hypsōsen en tē paroikia en gē Aigyptou, kai meta brachionos hypsēlou exēgagen autous ex autēs,

paragraphs.text: And for about the time of forty years as a nursing-father bare he them in the wilderness.
paragraphs.original: καί, ὡς τεσσερακονταετῆ χρόνον ἐτροποφόρησεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ,
paragraphs.translit: kai, hōs tesserakontaetē chronon etropophorēsen autous en tē erēmō,

paragraphs.text: And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave [them] their land for an inheritance, for about four hundred and fifty years:
paragraphs.original: καὶ καθελὼν ἔθνη ἑπτὰ ἐν γῇ Χανάαν κατεκληρονόμησεν τὴν γῆν αὐτῶν
paragraphs.translit: kai kathelōn ethnē hepta en gē Chanaan kateklēronomēsen tēn gēn autōn

paragraphs.text: and after these things he gave [them] judges until Samuel the prophet.
paragraphs.original: ὡς ἔτεσι τετρακοσίοις καὶ πεντήκοντα. καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἔδωκεν κριτὰς ἕως Σαμουὴλ τοῦ προφήτου.
paragraphs.translit: hōs etesi tetrakosiois kai pentēkonta. kai meta tauta edōken kritas heōs Samouēl tou prophētou.

paragraphs.text: And afterward they asked for a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for the space of forty years.
paragraphs.original: κἀκεῖθεν ᾐτήσαντο βασιλέα, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς τὸν Σαοὺλ υἱὸν Κίς, ἄνδρα ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, ἔτη τεσσεράκοντα·
paragraphs.translit: kakeithen ētēsanto basilea, kai edōken autois ho theos ton Saoul hyion Kis, andra ek phylēs Beniamin, etē tesserakonta·

paragraphs.text: And when he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king; to whom also he bare witness and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after My heart, who shall do all My will.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μεταστήσας αὐτὸν ἤγειρεν τὸν Δαυὶδ αὐτοῖς εἰς βασιλέα, ᾧ καὶ εἶπεν μαρτυρήσας· Εὗρον Δαυὶδ τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου, ὃς ποιήσει πάντα τὰ θελήματά μου.
paragraphs.translit: kai metastēsas auton ēgeiren ton Dauid autois eis basilea, hō kai eipen martyrēsas· Heuron Dauid ton tou Iessai, andra kata tēn kardian mou, hos poiēsei panta ta thelēmata mou.

paragraphs.text: Of this man`s seed hath God according to promise brought unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus;
paragraphs.original: τούτου ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ σπέρματος κατʼ ἐπαγγελίαν ἤγαγεν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ σωτῆρα Ἰησοῦν,
paragraphs.translit: toutou ho theos apo tou spermatos katʼ epangelian ēgagen tō Israēl sōtēra Iēsoun,

paragraphs.text: when John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
paragraphs.original: προκηρύξαντος Ἰωάννου πρὸ προσώπου τῆς εἰσόδου αὐτοῦ βάπτισμα μετανοίας παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραήλ.
paragraphs.translit: prokēryxantos Iōannou pro prosōpou tēs eisodou autou baptisma metanoias panti tō laō Israēl.

paragraphs.text: And as John was fulfilling his course, he said, What suppose ye that I am? I am not [he]. But behold, there cometh one after me the shoes of whose feet I am not worthy to unloose.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐπλήρου Ἰωάννης τὸν δρόμον, ἔλεγεν· Τί ἐμὲ ὑπονοεῖτε εἶναι; οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐγώ· ἀλλʼ ἰδοὺ ἔρχεται μετʼ ἐμὲ οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἄξιος τὸ ὑπόδημα τῶν ποδῶν λῦσαι.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de eplērou Iōannēs ton dromon, elegen· Ti eme hyponoeite einai; ouk eimi egō· allʼ idou erchetai metʼ eme hou ouk eimi axios to hypodēma tōn podōn lysai.

paragraphs.text: Brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you that fear God, to us is the word of this salvation sent forth.
paragraphs.original: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, υἱοὶ γένους Ἀβραὰμ καὶ οἱ ἐν ὑμῖν φοβούμενοι τὸν θεόν, ἡμῖν ὁ λόγος τῆς σωτηρίας ταύτης ἐξαπεστάλη.
paragraphs.translit: Andres adelphoi, hyioi genous Abraam kai hoi en hymin phoboumenoi ton theon, hēmin ho logos tēs sōtērias tautēs exapestalē.

paragraphs.text: For they that dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew him not, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath, fulfilled [them] by condemning [him].
paragraphs.original: οἱ γὰρ κατοικοῦντες ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες αὐτῶν τοῦτον ἀγνοήσαντες καὶ τὰς φωνὰς τῶν προφητῶν τὰς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκομένας κρίναντες ἐπλήρωσαν,
paragraphs.translit: hoi gar katoikountes en Ierousalēm kai hoi archontes autōn touton agnoēsantes kai tas phōnas tōn prophētōn tas kata pan sabbaton anaginōskomenas krinantes eplērōsan,

paragraphs.text: And though they found no cause of death [in him], yet asked they of Pilate that he should be slain.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μηδεμίαν αἰτίαν θανάτου εὑρόντες ᾐτήσαντο Πιλᾶτον ἀναιρεθῆναι αὐτόν·
paragraphs.translit: kai mēdemian aitian thanatou heurontes ētēsanto Pilaton anairethēnai auton·

paragraphs.text: And when they had fulfilled all things that were written of him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.
paragraphs.original: ὡς δὲ ἐτέλεσαν πάντα τὰ περὶ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένα, καθελόντες ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου ἔθηκαν εἰς μνημεῖον.
paragraphs.translit: hōs de etelesan panta ta peri autou gegrammena, kathelontes apo tou xylou ethēkan eis mnēmeion.

paragraphs.text: But God raised him from the dead:
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ θεὸς ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν·
paragraphs.translit: ho de theos ēgeiren auton ek nekrōn·

paragraphs.text: and he was seen for many days of them that came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses unto the people.
paragraphs.original: ὃς ὤφθη ἐπὶ ἡμέρας πλείους τοῖς συναναβᾶσιν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ, οἵτινες νῦν εἰσὶ μάρτυρες αὐτοῦ πρὸς τὸν λαόν.
paragraphs.translit: hos ōphthē epi hēmeras pleious tois synanabasin autō apo tēs Galilaias eis Ierousalēm, hoitines nyn eisi martyres autou pros ton laon.

paragraphs.text: And we bring you good tidings of the promise made unto the fathers,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελιζόμεθα τὴν πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας ἐπαγγελίαν γενομένην
paragraphs.translit: kai hēmeis hymas euangelizometha tēn pros tous pateras epangelian genomenēn

paragraphs.text: that God hath fulfilled the same unto our children, in that he raised up Jesus; as also it is written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ταύτην ὁ θεὸς ἐκπεπλήρωκεν τοῖς τέκνοις ἡμῶν ἀναστήσας Ἰησοῦν, ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ ψαλμῷ γέγραπται τῷ δευτέρῳ· Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε.
paragraphs.translit: hoti tautēn ho theos ekpeplērōken tois teknois hēmōn anastēsas Iēsoun, hōs kai en tō psalmō gegraptai tō deuterō· Hyios mou ei sy, egō sēmeron gegennēka se.

paragraphs.text: And as concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he hath spoken on this wise, I will give you the holy and sure [blessings] of David.
paragraphs.original: ὅτι δὲ ἀνέστησεν αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν μηκέτι μέλλοντα ὑποστρέφειν εἰς διαφθοράν, οὕτως εἴρηκεν ὅτι Δώσω ὑμῖν τὰ ὅσια Δαυὶδ τὰ πιστά.
paragraphs.translit: hoti de anestēsen auton ek nekrōn mēketi mellonta hypostrephein eis diaphthoran, houtōs eirēken hoti Dōsō hymin ta hosia Dauid ta pista.

paragraphs.text: Because he saith also in another [psalm], Thou wilt not give Thy Holy One to see corruption.
paragraphs.original: διότι καὶ ἐν ἑτέρῳ λέγει· Οὐ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν·
paragraphs.translit: dioti kai en heterō legei· Ou dōseis ton hosion sou idein diaphthoran·

paragraphs.text: For David, after he had in his own generation served the counsel of God, fell asleep, and was laid unto his fathers, and saw corruption:
paragraphs.original: Δαυὶδ μὲν γὰρ ἰδίᾳ γενεᾷ ὑπηρετήσας τῇ τοῦ θεοῦ βουλῇ ἐκοιμήθη καὶ προσετέθη πρὸς τοὺς πατέρας αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν διαφθοράν,
paragraphs.translit: Dauid men gar idia genea hypēretēsas tē tou theou boulē ekoimēthē kai prosetethē pros tous pateras autou kai eiden diaphthoran,

paragraphs.text: but he whom God raised up saw no corruption.
paragraphs.original: ὃν δὲ ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν οὐκ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
paragraphs.translit: hon de ho theos ēgeiren ouk eiden diaphthoran.

paragraphs.text: Be it known unto you therefore, brethren, that through this man is proclaimed unto you remission of sins:
paragraphs.original: γνωστὸν οὖν ἔστω ὑμῖν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὅτι διὰ τούτου ὑμῖν ἄφεσις ἁμαρτιῶν καταγγέλλεται, καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων ὧν οὐκ ἠδυνήθητε ἐν νόμῳ Μωϋσέως δικαιωθῆναι
paragraphs.translit: gnōston oun estō hymin, andres adelphoi, hoti dia toutou hymin aphesis hamartiōn katangelletai, kai apo pantōn hōn ouk ēdynēthēte en nomō Mōyseōs dikaiōthēnai

paragraphs.text: and by him every one that believeth is justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.
paragraphs.original: ἐν τούτῳ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων δικαιοῦται.
paragraphs.translit: en toutō pas ho pisteuōn dikaioutai.

paragraphs.text: Beware therefore, lest that come upon [you] which is spoken in the prophets:
paragraphs.original: βλέπετε οὖν μὴ ἐπέλθῃ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις·
paragraphs.translit: blepete oun mē epelthē to eirēmenon en tois prophētais·

paragraphs.text: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish; For I work a work in your days, A work which ye shall in no wise believe, if one declare it unto       you.
paragraphs.original: Ἴδετε, οἱ καταφρονηταί, καὶ θαυμάσατε καὶ ἀφανίσθητε, ὅτι ἔργον ἐργάζομαι ἐγὼ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ὑμῶν, ἔργον ὃ οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε ἐάν τις ἐκδιηγῆται ὑμῖν.
paragraphs.translit: Idete, hoi kataphronētai, kai thaumasate kai aphanisthēte, hoti ergon ergazomai egō en tais hēmerais hymōn, ergon ho ou mē pisteusēte ean tis ekdiēgētai hymin.

paragraphs.text: And as they went out, they besought that these words might be spoken to them the next sabbath.
paragraphs.original: Ἐξιόντων δὲ αὐτῶν παρεκάλουν εἰς τὸ μεταξὺ σάββατον λαληθῆναι αὐτοῖς τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα.
paragraphs.translit: Exiontōn de autōn parekaloun eis to metaxy sabbaton lalēthēnai autois ta rhēmata tauta.

paragraphs.text: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.
paragraphs.original: λυθείσης δὲ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἠκολούθησαν πολλοὶ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ τῶν σεβομένων προσηλύτων τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ, οἵτινες προσλαλοῦντες αὐτοῖς ἔπειθον αὐτοὺς προσμένειν τῇ χάριτι τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: lytheisēs de tēs synagōgēs ēkolouthēsan polloi tōn Ioudaiōn kai tōn sebomenōn prosēlytōn tō Paulō kai tō Barnaba, hoitines proslalountes autois epeithon autous prosmenein tē chariti tou theou.

paragraphs.text: And the next sabbath almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.
paragraphs.original: Τῷ δὲ ἐρχομένῳ σαββάτῳ σχεδὸν πᾶσα ἡ πόλις συνήχθη ἀκοῦσαι τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: Tō de erchomenō sabbatō schedon pasa hē polis synēchthē akousai ton logon tou kyriou.

paragraphs.text: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.
paragraphs.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τοὺς ὄχλους ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου καὶ ἀντέλεγον τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λαλουμένοις βλασφημοῦντες.
paragraphs.translit: idontes de hoi Ioudaioi tous ochlous eplēsthēsan zēlou kai antelegon tois hypo Paulou laloumenois blasphēmountes.

paragraphs.text: And Paul and Barnabas spake out boldly, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first be spoken to you. Seeing ye thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: παρρησιασάμενοί τε ὁ Παῦλος καὶ ὁ Βαρναβᾶς εἶπαν· Ὑμῖν ἦν ἀναγκαῖον πρῶτον λαληθῆναι τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐπειδὴ ἀπωθεῖσθε αὐτὸν καὶ οὐκ ἀξίους κρίνετε ἑαυτοὺς τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς, ἰδοὺ στρεφόμεθα εἰς τὰ ἔθνη·
paragraphs.translit: parrēsiasamenoi te ho Paulos kai ho Barnabas eipan· Hymin ēn anankaion prōton lalēthēnai ton logon tou theou· epeidē apōtheisthe auton kai ouk axious krinete heautous tēs aiōniou zōēs, idou strephometha eis ta ethnē·

paragraphs.text: For so hath the Lord commanded us, [saying], I have set thee for a light of the Gentiles, That thou shouldest be for salvation unto the uttermost part of       the earth.
paragraphs.original: οὕτως γὰρ ἐντέταλται ἡμῖν ὁ κύριος· Τέθεικά σε εἰς φῶς ἐθνῶν τοῦ εἶναί σε εἰς σωτηρίαν ἕως ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: houtōs gar entetaltai hēmin ho kyrios· Tetheika se eis phōs ethnōn tou einai se eis sōtērian heōs eschatou tēs gēs.

paragraphs.text: And as the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούοντα δὲ τὰ ἔθνη ἔχαιρον καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅσοι ἦσαν τεταγμένοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον·
paragraphs.translit: akouonta de ta ethnē echairon kai edoxazon ton logon tou kyriou, kai episteusan hosoi ēsan tetagmenoi eis zōēn aiōnion·

paragraphs.text: And the word of the Lord was spread abroad throughout all the region.
paragraphs.original: διεφέρετο δὲ ὁ λόγος τοῦ κυρίου διʼ ὅλης τῆς χώρας.
paragraphs.translit: diephereto de ho logos tou kyriou diʼ holēs tēs chōras.

paragraphs.text: But the Jews urged on the devout women of honorable estate, and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them out of their borders.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ Ἰουδαῖοι παρώτρυναν τὰς σεβομένας γυναῖκας τὰς εὐσχήμονας καὶ τοὺς πρώτους τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἐπήγειραν διωγμὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρναβᾶν, καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de Ioudaioi parōtrynan tas sebomenas gynaikas tas euschēmonas kai tous prōtous tēs poleōs kai epēgeiran diōgmon epi ton Paulon kai Barnaban, kai exebalon autous apo tōn horiōn autōn.

paragraphs.text: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἐκτιναξάμενοι τὸν κονιορτὸν τῶν ποδῶν ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ἦλθον εἰς Ἰκόνιον,
paragraphs.translit: hoi de ektinaxamenoi ton koniorton tōn podōn epʼ autous ēlthon eis Ikonion,

paragraphs.text: And the disciples were filled with joy with the Holy Spirit.
paragraphs.original: οἵ τε μαθηταὶ ἐπληροῦντο χαρᾶς καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
paragraphs.translit: hoi te mathētai eplērounto charas kai pneumatos hagiou.
